reviewer.note: the journal records an independent fresh-context reviewer per package but not a per-review identifier

note: Reconstructed after the fact on 2026-10-04 (CRV1) from the shared journal and commit history. Findings are only those the journal or the cited commits record; per-review reviewer identifiers and raw reports were not kept.

findings.summary: deeply nested JSON overflowed the stack in the std-only reader (depth limit missing)
lax JSON number grammar and duplicate keys were accepted
snapshot/ref ids with a leading dot or dot-dot could escape the intended directory
the sensor runner had no timeout and could hang the host
error text echoed filesystem paths and runner stderr
compile JSON reader had no depth limit; numbers not strict; \u escapes not hex-only; DEL not escaped; lone surrogate differed from the Python reference

SHA-256 padding edge lengths and CRLF/drift fixtures were not covered by vectors (hardening tests added; the journal counts the SHA-256 edge lengths among the 12 defects, no separate fix commit is isolated)
gate JSON reader accepted non-RFC 8259 numbers and non-hex \u escapes
each steps module (sensor, compile, gate) carries its own std-only JSON reader/writer; the same hardening had to be applied three times (ac3a599, e3e173e, 688c185)
findings.reason: Duplication was chosen so each lane could land independently with byte parity against its Python reference. A future divergence between the readers is the residual risk; parity tests against the Python references bound it today.
findings.tracking: not scheduled; consolidate into one shared module before the Rust shell (GT1A) or when a fourth reader is needed
